source.title: AEGD: adaptive gradient descent with energy

record.tranche_reason: Evaluates a new optimizer on CNN image-classification benchmarks and reports test accuracy relative to established optimizers, extending optimizer-generalization comparisons to AEGD.
record.gate_note: The paper's numerical optimizer comparisons on CIFAR image classification bear on V4. The reported performance-testing, clustering, and convergence results do not measure the claim versions. The excerpt gives no exact plotted test-accuracy values; Figure 5 reports them graphically.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares Adam and AdamW with momentum SGD on held-out image-classification accuracy. Appendix B.2 explicitly states that both generalize worse than SGDM in Figure 5, establishing a V4 result beyond the proposed optimizer's performance.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report preliminary evidence that AEGD or AEGDW can generalize better than SGDM, while emphasizing that AEGD's generalization remains insufficiently understood. They also explicitly conclude that Adam and AdamW generalize worse than SGDM in the main experiments.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces and evaluates a new energy-based adaptive optimizer, including an AEGD-specific decoupled weight-decay variant; compares with Adam, AdamW and SGDM rather than reproducing the cited optimizer studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance changes with training time and learning-rate decay: Adam/AdamW lead early, while AEGD/AEGDW outperform by epoch 150 after the scheduled decay.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed AEGD and AEGDW optimizers reportedly exceed SGDM test accuracy by approximately 1% in the two main CNN experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Energy-based adaptive optimization can outperform momentum SGD under the tested image-classification recipes.

record.problems: The authors call the neural-network generalization results preliminary. Exact test-accuracy values are only plotted, with no uncertainty estimates reported. The paper fine-tunes base step sizes for each algorithm and does not report a random-label or memorization-capacity check.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-bearing results omitted. Other optimization benchmarks and the MNIST/CIFAR-10 MLP and CifarNet results compare AEGD variants with SGDM but do not test V4's stated image-classification and language-benchmark adaptive-optimizer comparison in the reported main experiment; the paper's prose supplies no exact plotted accuracies for those additional results.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Controlled convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local connectivity.

Language benchmarks, broader hyperparameter tuning, switching Adam to SGD, and whether worse held-out performance accompanies equal or better training performance. The text does not resolve whether AdamW improves on Adam.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations that remove large-batch penalties.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The proposed limits_scope verdict confuses early optimizer performance and the new method's advantage with the final Adam-versus-SGDM comparison. Appendix B.2 supplies the decisive direct statement. Additional MNIST and CifarNet experiments are already declared in rows_left_out and report the proposed methods' performance; no undeclared claim-bearing result requires a missing entry. No numerical curves or uncertainty estimates can be recovered from the supplied figure captions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Generalization as network width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Comparison is limited to the paper's listed CNN benchmarks and optimizer recipes; no language benchmarks, broader tuning comparison, or Adam-to-SGD switch is tested.
Large versus small batch training and batch-size effects.
Sharpness or other measured properties tracking the train-test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

relationships.condition: Adam and AdamW versus SGDM on ResNet-56/CIFAR-10 and SqueezeNet/CIFAR-100, using 200 epochs, batch size 128, weight decay 10^-4 and learning-rate decay after 150 epochs.
relationships.reason: Appendix B.2 explicitly states that Adam(W) generalizes worse than SGDM in Figure 5, covering R1–R4; base learning rates were tuned separately with other settings prescribed.
relationships.display_finding: The reported worse test performance for Adam and AdamW than momentum SGD after separate learning-rate tuning remains unverified.
